dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected every graph file's sizes/headers/node-name conventions and the reference alignment; quantified baselines (reference NC=1.0/S3≈0.248, degree-sort DM-HS≈0.269) rather than acting blind.
Explicitly reasoned that topology drives S3 while the reference alignment drives NC, and that the two deliverables carry different constraints — deriving pinning/locking strategy per deliverable.
Researched node-ID meaning (NCBI/BioGRID orthologs, tested internet), then identified filenames as the SANA benchmark and downloaded/built the published SANA aligner — active method research.
Evaluated the published SANA method against concrete instances: its S3 vs EC objectives, temperature schedules, runtime cost, and lock option for preserving NC, alongside its own annealer.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized both network pairs, inspected the reference alignment, quantified what baselines score, and identified the exact structural signal each threshold rewards (topology for S3, reference-overlap for NC) with differing per-deliverable constraints — matching anchor 8. It went further by researching orthology data and locating/building the published SANA aligner and evaluating its objectives/runtime against the concrete instances (anchor 10 territory). It stops just short of a full 10 because the method evaluation largely converged on SANA plus a custom annealer rather than comparing several distinct published aligners.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: From the outset the agent separates the pipeline into distinct stages: parse graphs (analyze_align.py), test baselines (test_baselines.py), and build an independent scorer (score_align.py) — treating parsing, scoring, and alignment generation as separable sub-goals rather than one undifferentiated 'write the file' push.

Builds/uses the scorer BEFORE optimizing against it, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their numeric done-criteria (yeast S3>=0.55 & NC>=0.30 vs DM-HS S3>=0.32). Explicitly recognizes the NC-constraint as the distinguishing difficulty of the yeast task ('understand if NC is the limiting factor').

Effort budgeting by difficulty: once yeast passes (S3≈0.562, NC≈0.387) the agent copies it to final and redirects ALL remaining effort to the harder S3-only DM-HS deliverable, gating each new candidate on measured improvement ('update final only if improved').

Sustained milestone gating on measured scores: repeatedly waits for a run, scores /app/DM-HS.*.align against the numeric 0.32 target and against current best, and only promotes to /app/DM-HS.align if it beats the prior best — a clear done-check tied to the threshold.

Consistent fallback branches per milestone: when an approach plateaus below threshold the agent has a pre-stated 'if this fails, try X' (EC objective, esim, cold seed, exhaustive opt_all), each measured against the numeric target before advancing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 8: it establishes explicit ordered milestones (parse → build independent scorer → baseline scores → optimize to numeric threshold), builds the scorer before optimizing against it, and tracks both deliverables with their respective numeric done-criteria throughout. It also shows the anchor-10 markers — budgeting effort across deliverables by difficulty (front-loading the NC-constrained yeast task, then concentrating all remaining runs on the S3-only fly task once yeast passed), fallback branches per milestone, and gating each candidate on measured scores before promoting it to the final file. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because the milestone hierarchy is emergent/reactive across the per-step Analysis/Plan notes rather than laid out as a crisp explicit hierarchy up front.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Built analyze_align.py and test_baselines.py to parse graphs and validate the yeast alignment; at step 4 (line 17) caught that an earlier S3 was invalid because the alignment was read in file order rather than Yeast2KReduced node order — guarding against a mapping/ordering scorer bug.
Sanity-checked scorer against the reference alignment: 'copied yeast reference gives NC=1.0 but only S3≈0.248' — confirming NC≈1.0 and a plausible S3, the classic anchor-8 validation.
Created independent Python score_align.py explicitly to validate candidate S3/NC separately from the C++ optimizer's internal scoring, then used it as the recurring feedback loop.

score_align.py invoked on essentially every candidate (dozens of runs) as the optimization objective and stopping test, with precise threshold comparisons (e.g. distinguishing S3=0.543 vs the 0.55 target).

Final verification of injectivity, exact line counts, and format ('valid/injective with correct line counts'); correctly reported yeast passes (S3≈0.562, NC≈0.387) and DM-HS falls short (S3≈0.296) rather than assuming success.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented faithful S3 and NC scorers, validated injectivity/coverage/format, and — matching the anchor-8 description — sanity-checked the scorer by confirming the reference alignment yields NC=1.0 with a sensible S3, caught an ordering bug that would have corrupted scoring, and used the score as the optimization objective and stopping test throughout. It stops short of anchor 10 because there is no evidence of explicit edge-case testing of the E2_aligned denominator or hand-verification against double-counting, so it lands solidly at 8.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Early and repeatedly states exact current scores vs targets: yeast copied ref NC=1.0 but S3≈0.248 < 0.55; DM-HS baselines ≈0.269. Enumerates multiple candidates with their S3/NC, showing continuous distance-to-threshold awareness.

Explicitly recognizes plateaus ('plateaued at S3≈0.445', 'local optimum at S3≈0.46') and tracks best current candidates per deliverable (highpin S3≈0.457/NC≈0.333, topology S3≈0.463/NC~0, DM-HS 0.269), deciding approaches have stopped yielding gains.

Runs score_align.py with several candidate files simultaneously — a best-so-far comparison mechanism — and only copies a candidate into /app/DM-HS.align or /app/y2kr-SC.align when it improves on the incumbent.
Monitors the long 600s DM-HS run's score progression (0.226→0.244→0.266→0.280→0.288→0.291) against incumbent 0.296 and correctly decides to preserve the existing best rather than adopt the worse run.

Final analyses accurately summarize: yeast passes both (S3≈0.562, NC≈0.387), DM-HS best-found 0.296 still below 0.32; refuses to mark complete while DM-HS falls short, and notes the exhaustive optimizer found no improvement — never loses the plot over the long horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a precise, continuous picture of best-so-far S3/NC per deliverable, compares candidates head-to-head, recognizes plateaus and regressions, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — matching the level-8 anchor fully and much of level-10 (logged score progression, distinguishing 'still improving' from 'stuck', keeping the incumbent when new runs are worse). It falls just short of a perfect 10 because it sometimes waited out runs already tracking below the incumbent rather than cutting them earlier, though this was reasoned rather than blind looping.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Diagnosed that the copied reference gave NC=1.0 but S3≈0.248 (below 0.55), correctly identified S3 as the shortfall, and pivoted from a trivial copy to a custom C++ simulated-annealer pinning 30% of nodes for NC — a materially different tactic driven by the observed metric gap.

When the annealer plateaued (~0.445-0.46), tried a sequence of distinct tactics each prompted by analysis of WHY: low-degree pins → high-degree pins, topology-only, exhaustive best-move local search, then a hybrid keeping the low-E2a target subset while forcing NC pairs, then swap-only annealing. Clear hypothesis-driven variation of algorithm/objective.

Recognized homegrown heuristics were stuck and pivoted to external signals: tested NCBI ortholog name-overlap seeding, abandoned it quickly when IDs turned out to be BioGRID not Entrez, then located, downloaded and compiled the SANA benchmark aligner — a decisive strategy switch that kept prior gains as seeds.

Diagnosed NC-low vs S3-low tradeoff explicitly: switched from hard locks to SANA's -nc objective with the reference true-alignment, then tuned the NC weight 0.5→0.1→0.18→0.14 to bracket the constraints, discovered nc-light passes S3 but fails NC while nc-018 passes NC but fails S3 by 0.0003, and did a greedy repair — combining complementary signals for the yeast constraint set until it passed (S3≈0.562, NC≈0.387).

For DM-HS (S3-only), tried EC objective, mixed S3+EC, S3+ICS, NATALIE sequence-similarity files, seeded/cold hill-climb optimizers, and exhaustive opt_all — many targeted pivots. Toward the end there is some grinding: repeated long fresh runs of the same custom optimizer that plateaued near 0.296, kept only if improved (dead-end abandonment preserved but slightly repetitive).

dimensions.reasoning: Across the whole arc the agent repeatedly and deliberately changed algorithm, seeding signal, and objective in direct response to observed shortfalls, forming explicit hypotheses (NC low → reference/-nc seeding; S3 low → topological local search; E2a high → ICS), abandoning dead ends fast (orthologs), and preserving accumulated gains by seeding new runs from best files — matching the level-10 anchor for the yeast constraint set. It falls just short of a pure 10 because the DM-HS end-game devolved into several near-identical long optimizer reruns with little fresh diagnosis of the plateau, so I place it at 9.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
